Playing a positive role in the communities where we operate is equally important to us. Meta is hiring two Regional Managers to lead teams within our data center Community Engagement organization, with a preference for one based in the Western United States and one in the Eastern United States. vacancies.title: Director, Product Management - Agents and Intelligence
vacancies.description:
AI is creating effectively unlimited demand for insight while the traditional ways of producing it remain constrained. Meta cannot meet that demand by asking people to write every query, investigate every fast mover, or manually assemble every analysis. We need intelligent systems that can do the routine work at scale while enabling people to focus their creativity on the questions only they can ask.

The Data Analytics Tooling & Agents (DATA) organization is building that future. We are looking for a senior product lead to own the Intelligence & Execution layer: the agentic capabilities that understand intent, reason over Meta’s data and context, plan and execute analytical work, learn from feedback, and take safe action.

Your goal is to make these capabilities durable across models and interfaces, and to make AI the default way people across Meta turn questions into decisions. Success means materially improving the quality, complexity, and impact of the work our agents can complete quarter over quarter.

Responsibilities:
Set the intelligence and execution strategy.Define the roadmap and investment plan for agent reasoning, orchestration, skills, memory, tool use, and workflow execution across analytics. Move from assistance to autonomous outcomes.Enable agents to complete increasingly complex work end to end—from querying and interpretation to root-cause analysis, simulation, proactive insight generation, and appropriately governed action. Build reusable agent capabilities. Create shared skills and execution patterns that teams can compose across domains, rather than bespoke agents that solve one workflow at a time. Make the system improve continuously. Partner closely with the context and evaluation teams so production feedback, hard evals, and failure analysis translate into better reasoning and execution, not simply better demos. Choose the right intelligence for the job. Make clear product and technical tradeoffs across frontier models, specialized or distilled models, deterministic systems, latency, cost, and quality. Lead end-to-end execution.Align engineering, data science, data engineering, design, research, privacy, and product teams across the agent experience, data foundations, and operational controls. Define and meet the quality bar.Own measures of task success, answer quality, analytical complexity, productivity, autonomous insight impact, reliability, and efficiency.

12+ years of experience in Product Management and/or equivalent relevant experience 12+ years of experience working collaboratively with engineering, design and user research teams 8+ years of experience hiring, managing, and developing both individual contributors and senior leaders Critical thinking/analytical leadership experience Experience presenting to senior executive audiences BA/BS in Computer Science or related field Experience working with Agentic products and workflows (e.g. evals, semantic layer, skills) Experience working on Analytics/enterprise cloud data platforms Experience building 0-1 products, platform/ecosystem products, or marketplaces Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements) Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews) Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

vacancies.title: Finance & Business Operations Manager, WhatsApp

Finance and Business Planning is a highly mission driven organization. Our mission is to enable Meta to plan, prioritize, and execute as effectively as possible. Almost nothing about this work has been done before. Robotics law is largely unwritten, and the questions this role takes on will often have no precedent, no settled guidance, and no playbook to work from. We are looking for an attorney who finds that energizing rather than unsettling: someone who reasons from first principles, gets comfortable fast with hard technical subject matter, and can chart a path forward through ambiguity. vacancies.title: Research Scientist, Server Demand
vacancies.description:
Meta runs one of the largest server fleets on earth, and every product bet (AI training, ranking, inference, storage) turns into a demand for compute that we must forecast, shape, and match to a physical supply of servers, racks, power, and data center space. As the senior technical owner of Server Demand Planning, you own the demand side of that equation and close the loop with supply: you forecast long- and near-term server capacity demand by rack/hardware type and region, and you build the operations-research models that match that demand to supply so we land the right servers, in the right place, at the right time. You set the modeling approach for the function, decide when to ship a production-grade optimization system versus a fast lightweight model to unblock a decision, and act as the connective tissue between product/service capacity owners, capacity engineering, supply chain, data center planning, and finance.

Responsibilities:
Own the multi-horizon server/MW demand forecast long range (2-5+ years), by resource type and DC supply requirements. Aggregate and normalize demand signals from short term demand and product groups, into a single trusted statistical long term demand plan. Formulate and solve the demand-supply matching problem using operations-research models that reconcile forecasted demand with hardware roadmaps, cooling, lead times, and power constraints to inform the Plan of Record. Build across the full modeling spectrum: production-grade optimization and forecasting systems and prototype models and heuristics that answer a leadership question or unblock a decision. Set functional standards: define the operating model, bridge short- and long-term forecasts, track accuracy and supply-matching metrics, and bridge forecast-to-actual gaps. Partner with IDC engineering, site selection, and hardware strategy teams to align next-generation data center designs, rack sizing, and hardware roadmaps with demand, eliminating stranded power, cooling, and space capacity.

Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience 7+ years applying operations research / management science to real planning problems in demand planning, capacity planning, supply-demand matching, network optimization, or inventory MS in a quantitative field (Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Applied Math, Statistics, CS, or related), or equivalent experience Deep operations-research toolkit: mathematical optimization (LP, MILP, stochastic/robust optimization), simulation, queuing theory, and probabilistic/statistical forecasting Demonstrated ability to build BOTH production-grade models/systems (deployed, maintained, driving real decisions) AND lightweight/prototype models delivered fast under ambiguity Strong demand-to-supply matching experience: reconciling forecasted demand against constrained supply, lead times, and inventory Fluency with optimization solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, or OR-Tools) and with SQL + Python for modeling, analysis, and pipelines PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Management Science, or a related quantitative field Direct experience with server/compute or data center capacity planning at hyperscale Statistical/ML forecasting depth (time series, hierarchical/probabilistic forecasting, forecast reconciliation) Experience with planning platforms (Kinaxis, SAP IBP, o9, Blue Yonder, Demantra, E2open) and internal capacity tools (MCP/ICPC, Capacity Explorer) Publications, patents, or recognized technical leadership in OR / optimization / forecasting

The SDE team sits at the critical juncture between innovative product design and scalable, high-volume manufacturing — bridging upstream development (product design, material selection) and downstream integration (FATP). You will take ownership of the technical and operational complexities of ramping robotics products from prototype through mass production.

This is a unique opportunity to shape how Meta's next-generation robotics hardware gets built at scale. You'll work hands-on with suppliers, develop manufacturing processes, drive quality systems, and collaborate deeply with Hardware, Industrial Design, Process, Sourcing, FATP Operations.

**Component & Module Scope**

**Electromechanical:** Motors, Actuators, Gear Train

**Mechanical:** Enclosures, Housings, Structural Components, Thermal Management, Softgoods

**Electronics & Sensing:** Cables, Wire Harness, Connectors, PCBA/FPC, Tactile Sensing, Battery, Display

**Audio & Vision:** Audio Modules, Camera/Sensor/Lens, Display, Optical Covers

Your team defines how Triton and lower-level DSLs map onto MTIA hardware, shaping language extensions, target-specific optimizations, and the kernel authoring experience used by kernel engineers, product groups, and model teams across Meta. The work spans open-source contributions and internal compiler development, directly influences ISA and architecture roadmap decisions, and carries top-level executive visibility as a key AI infrastructure initiative. The team culture celebrates deep technical contributions with extensive knowledge-sharing, including external conference talks and published research.

Responsibilities:
You will drive the development of the DSL compiler toolchain, including ML compiler integration, GEMM and non-GEMM kernel enablement, collectives support, and next-generation low-level DSLs. You will lead teams of engineers and technical leaders delivering large-scale projects across compiler infrastructure, kernel libraries, and production deployment on multiple accelerator generations You will stay technically engaged, contributing hands-on through AI tools to evaluate the technical direction and quality across your teams. You will form trusted cross-functional partnerships with hardware/architecture, kernel, runtime, framework, and model teams while actively shaping strategy and roadmap, and you will balance near-term deployment commitments against long-term compiler investments. You will build and mentor engineers into AI-era leaders while maintaining high engineering craft standards

In this role, you will collaborate with software engineering, data science, and product management teams to design/build scalable data solutions across Meta to optimize growth, strategy, and user experience for our 3 billion plus users, as well as our internal employee community.

You will be at the forefront of identifying and solving some of the most interesting data challenges at a scale few companies can match. By joining Meta, you will become part of a data engineering community dedicated to skill development and career growth in data engineering and beyond.

Facebook helps more than 3 billion people around the world connect, share, and build community. From reconnecting with old friends to discovering local groups, marketplaces, and creators, the Facebook app is where people come to find the people and things they care about. As one of the world's largest consumer products, Facebook is continuously reinventing itself, investing in video, AI-powered discovery, creators, groups, and marketplace experiences that keep the app vital for the next generation of users.

We are looking for a seasoned, visionary product marketing leader to lead the transformation of Facebook's product marketing organization and the global team of product marketers behind it. This leader will set the vision and strategy for how Facebook grows relevance with the next generation and delivers more value to core users, influencing product strategies and roadmaps, and driving product launches and go-to-market in the US and key global markets. Success looks like moving Facebook from an app that's “around” to an app that's essential.

The ideal candidate will be able to build and drive product strategy, with a deep understanding of the industry competitive landscape, trends, and business models. They will bring the operational rigor and organizational leadership to align a large, global team and its cross-functional partners behind a single, ambitious agenda.

Responsibilities:

Set the vision and strategy for how Facebook grows relevance with the next generation and delivers deeper value to core users, including the positioning frameworks that guide Facebook across existing and new markets and user segments. Have a pulse on the consumer and on culture, and marry the two with business and product strategy to develop marketing that moves consumers at scale, influencing product strategy and roadmaps as the voice of the consumer. Shape the Facebook narrative: partner with product to make it true, and partner with cross-functional teams to land it with consumers and in culture. As a technical owner within Server Demand Planning, you drive server demand forecasting and demand-supply matching for your area and close on feasible supply requirements: you forecast near- and long-term server capacity demand by rack/hardware type and region, and you build the operations research models that match that demand to supply so we land the right long-term DC & hardware infra requirements, in the right place, at the right time. You choose the right modeling approach for the problems you own, deciding when to ship a production-grade optimization system versus a fast lightweight model to unblock a decision, and you partner closely across product/service capacity owners, capacity engineering, supply chain, data center planning, and finance.

Responsibilities:
Own and drive a multi-horizon server/MW demand forecast (near term through 2-5+ years), producing trusted, reproducible release to inform decisions Aggregate and normalize demand signals from short-term demand and product groups into a single trusted statistical long-term demand plan Formulate and solve the demand-supply matching problem using operations-research models that reconcile forecasted demand with hardware roadmaps, cooling, lead times, and power constraints to inform the Plan of Record Build across the full modeling spectrum: production-grade optimization and forecasting systems and prototype models and heuristics that answer a leadership question or unblock a decision Partner with IDC engineering, site selection, and hardware strategy teams to align next-generation data center designs, rack sizing, and hardware roadmaps with demand, eliminating stranded power, cooling, and space capacity

Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience 6+ years applying operations research / management science to real planning problems in demand planning, capacity planning, supply-demand matching, network optimization, or inventory MS in a quantitative field (Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Applied Math, Statistics, CS, or related), or equivalent experience Deep operations-research toolkit: mathematical optimization (LP, MILP, stochastic/robust optimization), simulation, queuing theory, and probabilistic/statistical forecasting Demonstrated ability to build BOTH production-grade models/systems (deployed, maintained, driving real decisions) AND lightweight/prototype models delivered fast under ambiguity Experience with demand-to-supply matching: reconciling forecasted demand against constrained supply, lead times, and inventory Fluency with optimization solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, or OR-Tools) and with SQL + Python for modeling, analysis, and pipelines Direct experience with server/compute or data center capacity planning at hyperscale PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Management Science, or a related quantitative field Experience with planning platforms (Kinaxis, SAP IBP, o9, Blue Yonder, Demantra, E2open) and internal capacity tools (MCP/ICPC, Capacity Explorer) Statistical/ML forecasting depth (time series, hierarchical/probabilistic forecasting, forecast reconciliation) Publications, patents, or recognized technical leadership in OR / optimization / forecasting

Product leadership: You will use data to shape product development, quantify new opportunities, identify upcoming challenges, and ensure the products we build bring value to people, businesses, and Meta. Communication and influence: You won't simply present data, but tell data-driven stories. You will convince and influence your partners using clear insights and recommendations. You will build credibility through structure and clarity, and be a trusted strategic partner.

-------

En tant que Data Scientist chez Meta, vous façonnerez l'avenir des produits destinés aux personnes et aux entreprises que nous construisons dans toute notre famille d'applications (Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, Oculus). En appliquant vos compétences techniques, votre esprit d'analyse et votre intuition en matière de produits à l'un des ensembles de données les plus riches au monde, vous contribuerez à définir les expériences que nous construisons pour des milliards de personnes et des centaines de millions d'entreprises dans le monde entier. Vous collaborerez sur une large gamme de problématiques liées aux produits et à l’activité avec de nombreux partenaires interfonctionnels, notamment les équipes produit, ingénierie, recherche, ingénierie des données, marketing, ventes, finance, etc.  Vous utiliserez des données et des analyses pour identifier et résoudre les plus grands défis du développement de produits. Vous aurez une influence dans la stratégie du produit et sur les décisions d'investissement à l'aide de données, vous serez focalisé sur l'impact et vous travaillerez en collaboration avec d'autres équipes. En rejoignant Meta, vous ferez partie d'une communauté d'analystes dédiée au développement des compétences et à l'évolution de carrière dans l'analyse et au-delà.

Direction du produit : Vous utiliserez les données pour façonner le développement des produits, quantifier les nouvelles opportunités, identifier les défis à venir et veiller à ce que les produits que nous construisons apportent de la valeur aux personnes, aux entreprises et à Meta. Vous aiderez vos équipes partenaires à prioriser ce qu’il faut construire, à définir des objectifs et à comprendre l’écosystème de leur produit.

Analytique : Vous guiderez les équipes à l'aide de données et d'informations. Vous vous concentrerez sur l'élaboration d'hypothèses et utiliserez un ensemble varié d'approches analytiques rigoureuses, de méthodologies différentes, de cadres et d'approches techniques pour les tester.

Communication et influence : Vous ne présenterez pas simplement des données, mais raconterez des histoires basées sur des données. Vous serez amené à convaincre et à influencer vos partenaires grâce à des informations et des recommandations claires. vacancies.title: ASIC Package Engineer
vacancies.description:
Meta is looking for an experienced ASIC Package Engineer to join its ASIC Packaging team. This role owns the technology development and qualification readiness of the package-to-board attach process for Meta's custom AI/ML and networking silicon — the critical interface where a larger than reticle sized, large-body advanced package meets the motherboard Meta designs. The engineer will lead the development and optimization of package interaction with board attach processes. The Meta Infrastructure team designs, builds, brings up, tests, and integrates custom and general-purpose silicon-based hardware systems that power Meta's platforms, deployed in data centers worldwide. Designs are published through the Open Compute Project Foundation. We are building a deep competency in packaging technology to support the rapid development of custom silicon and to develop scalable packaging solutions that are optimal for our next-generation AI/ML products and system-level performance. As die sizes grow past 3.3x reticle and packages move to lidless/lidded and asymmetric stackups, board technology development for next gen ASIC is very important to achieve desired yield due to challenges with package warpage, thermo-mechanical stresses, and solder-joint reliability. The person in this role serves as the primary packaging expert for package to board technology development, working shoulder-to-shoulder with Product Quality Engineering (PQE), Supplier Quality Engineering (SQE), and module design teams to turn it into a fully qualified, statistically controlled, high-yield manufacturing process.

Responsibilities:
Own package-to-board interaction technology development for Meta's large-body advanced packages — how the package, substrate, and PCB behave together through assembly and in the field Characterize and mitigate package warpage and coplanarity across the reflow window for large-body and lidless packages Drive board-level reliability (BLR) strategy for ASIC packages in partnership with quality teams — thermal cycling, drop/shock, bend, and vibration Define and execute mechanical and electrical test vehicle (MTV/ETV) strategies to de-risk package-board interaction ahead of A0 silicon availability, including solder-joint evaluation by X-ray, cross-section, and dye-and-pry at the ODM Represent package-board interaction and board-assembly constraints in silicon/package/PCB/system co-design and product design reviews Collaborate with package design and module design teams to ensure design for manufacturability (DFM) considerations are incorporated into package and board development Develop and implement package-board interaction process specifications, design rules, and manufacturing guidelines for new package technologies Evaluate and qualify new package-board interaction equipment, materials, and processes to support technology roadmap requirements Partner with PQE, SQE, and ARD teams to establish quality standards, qualification criteria, and reliability requirements for package-board interaction processes Establish statistical process control (SPC) methodologies and yield improvement initiatives for package-board interaction assembly operations Own package-board interaction content in FMEAs, control plans, and key-characteristic definitions; support ODM line qualification and control-run gates with PQE Create, conduct, and analyze Designs of Experiments (DOE) for package-board interaction development and sustaining activities Drive supplier engagement and qualification for package-board interaction-related materials and equipment

Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience Master's degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience 8+ years of experience in semiconductor packaging with direct ownership of package-to-board assembly and reliability; package-board interaction process engineering or electronics manufacturing background Experience with package board technology processes including solder paste printing, pick-and-place, reflow soldering, and inspection methods Experience working with package assembly and ODM suppliers and driving process qualification and yield improvement programs Experience with failure analysis techniques for solder joint reliability and package-board interaction-related defects Experience collaborating with quality engineering teams (PQE/SQE) to establish process controls and qualification requirements Experience with statistical process control, process capability analysis, and Design of Experiments Willingness to travel internationally, typically once per quarter Experience with reflow temperature profiling, solder alloy and paste material selection, and low-temperature solder processes Experience with AI/HPC or networking hardware at data-center scale Experience with high-temperature warpage characterization and thermo-mechanical or finite element modeling (FEM) of packages and solder joints Hands-on experience with SPI, AOI, and X-ray inspection systems and associated data analysis Experience with large-body FCBGA, flip-chip, and 2.5D/3D advanced packages and their interaction with board-assembly constraints Master's degree or PhD in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline Knowledge of packaging and assembly industry standards Experience with ODM, CM/EMS, OSAT, and substrate supplier engagement and audit

Security Foundations is Meta's first-line-of-defense technology organization, owning the controls that manage security risk across the company. We're looking for a Security Engineer Lead to scope, design, and champion security solutions company-wide across the domains we support.

This is a breadth role. Each domain below has its own engineering leaders and managers — you will set technical direction across them rather than owning one. The hardest problems in this space does not sit inside a single domain. Agent identity and authorization, for example, spans identity and access, product authentication, AI security, and cloud simultaneously. Finding those problems and getting them solved once, coherently, is central to this role.

The domains you'll influence:

Identity and Access Management — the authorization layer every Meta system depends on, serving tens of billions of access checks per second

Cryptography and Data Security — including Meta's post-quantum migration and Encryption at Rest

Product Identity and Access — authentication for billions of end users

AI Security — the controls protecting Meta's frontier AI products

Cloud Security — securing Meta's footprint across public cloud and third-party compute providers, including identity, network egress, and posture management

Asset Management — authoritative security risk classification for assets across the company

Scope and complexity:

-Security Foundations is a cross-functional organization of engineers, analysts, and product managers, partnering closely with hundreds of engineers elsewhere in the company.
-The role spans a large set of technical domains: Meta's products and custom technology stack, commercial off-the-shelf software (e.g. Active Directory), and commercial IaaS/PaaS services. Familiarity with industry best practices and relevant regulatory frameworks — plus the ability to translate between those frameworks and deeply technical software engineers.

What success looks like in the first year:

-A defensible, company-wide view of the highest-risk items across these domains, with named owners and real threat models — not a list.
-At least one shared platform or control adopted broadly enough to measurably change the company's risk posture.
-Security tradeoffs represented credibly at the VP and C-level, with decisions made rather than deferred.

Responsibilities:

Determine the highest-risk items across these domains company-wide, then lead development of detailed threat models and solutions. Define how AI agents are identified, authorized, and audited across Meta's infrastructure — a space where neither existing industry practice nor our own human-centric models are sufficient. Navigate tradeoffs between security and friction or cost, so the company can keep moving fast securely. Drive solution design, including technical architecture, and lead implementation as needed. Build partnerships across security, infrastructure, corporate engineering, and legal — then use those partnerships to translate ambiguous business and regulatory requirements into well-articulated tradeoffs between "secure the company and our users" and "slow the company down.". Represent those tradeoffs credibly to senior leadership, including VPs and C-level executives (CTO, CISO), to drive decisions.

vacancies.description:
The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. 

In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team works on technologies that help people hear and communicate better in everyday life, from spatial audio to hearing assistance on AI glasses. Recent work includes Conversation Focus, which helps people hear the person they're talking to in noisy environments. As wearable devices become part of daily life, understanding how people actually listen, attend, and communicate in real-world settings is central to building audio experiences that adapt to each person.

We are looking for interns who want to model how people listen and communicate in the real world. Using multimodal, egocentric data from wearable devices (eye and head movement, speech and vocal behavior, gesture, and the acoustic scene), the intern will build models that infer listening and communication states such as auditory attention, listening effort, and conversational engagement. Ground truth for these states is often sparse or ambiguous. The goal is to inform hearing assistance and audio technologies that adapt to the listener.

The role suits candidates with a background in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, who want to work at the intersection of those fields. Successful candidates will combine strong quantitative and machine learning skills with an understanding of human hearing and communication. Specific projects will be designed with successful applicants to match their skills and experience to current research needs. 

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities:
Develop novel machine learning and statistical models that infer listening and communication behavior from multimodal wearable data (for example gaze, head movement, vocal cues, and turn-taking dynamics), with applications to hearing assistance. Relate model outputs to established hearing science measures, such as speech intelligibility, listening effort, and self-reported communication difficulty, to validate what the models capture. Design data collection strategies, benchmarks, and metrics for models trained on limited or ambiguous ground truth, including data from listeners with and without hearing loss. Design, run, and analyze human subjects experiments in laboratory and naturalistic listening environments. Collaborate with researchers and engineers across hearing science, audio signal processing, machine learning, and perception science. Communicate the research agenda, progress, and full analyses of results.

vacancies.title: People Service Delivery Lead

The People Service Delivery (PSD) team's mission is to run a high-performing, people-focused service delivery organization. Leading with care and empathy, we develop efficient processes, systems, and programs. We aim to ensure employees feel heard and have the resources and support they need during the most important moments so they can do impactful work. 

The People Service Delivery Lead sits at the intersection of people operations domain expertise and hands-on engineering. This role owns large-scale transformation programs end to end, and, unlike a traditional program role, also contributes to designing and building the solutions those programs depend on. This lead reads HR, payroll, and people-operations workflows fluently, identifies where the seams and inefficiencies are, and then helps architect tooling solutions that close them.

Working closely with leaders across People Operations, executive sponsors, engineering, and other key XFN stakeholders, this lead challenges assumptions and the status quo to improve processes, reduce barriers, and mitigate risks. Much of the work is greenfield: problems arrive without a playbook, and this lead defines the path as they walk it. This person does not need to have the “correct” answer to everything. What matters is the ability to quickly drive the conversation toward a productive solution by bringing together the right people, process, and technology, including building a working prototype when that is the fastest way to create clarity.

A key expectation of this role is to be an active driver of AI adoption and creative problem-solving in operations. This lead looks for opportunities to responsibly use AI and automation to reduce manual work, improve consistency, accelerate resolution times, and enhance the employee experience while ensuring strong governance, quality, and appropriate handling of sensitive information.

vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern – Robotics, World Models & Embodied AI (PhD)
vacancies.description:
Meta Reality Labs Research (RL Research) brings together a world-class R&D team of researchers and engineers with the shared goal of developing AI, Robotics, and AR/VR technology across the spectrum. The Surreal Spatial AI group is seeking Research Scientist Interns to help build the machine perception, 3D generative systems, and control technology that allow robotic agents and AI systems to perceive, understand, reason about, and interact with the world around them.

Our research puts multi-modal generative world models at the core of machine perception and robotic control, using data from egocentric devices such as Project Aria alongside data from physical robots. As an intern, you will work with our research scientists and engineers on robot foundation models, including world action models (WAMs) and vision-language-action models (VLAs). Projects can span several research streams, including exploring novel architectures, grounding these models in 3D, learning action and goal representations, and integrating new sensor modalities such as touch.

Interns in this role are proficient in research areas such as action-conditioned world models, 3D computer vision, representation learning, learning from human video and demonstrations, cross-embodiment transfer, tactile sensing, reinforcement learning, and dexterous manipulation. You should have a keen interest in producing new, open science that makes embodied agents more intelligent.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities:
Perform fundamental and applied research at the intersection of multi-modal generative AI, predictive world modeling, embodied reasoning, and robotic manipulation. Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to explore novel architectures for robot foundation models, such as WAMs and VLAs. Ground robot foundation models in 3D, using 3D computer vision and scene understanding. Develop action and goal representations that transfer across embodiments, from human video to different robots. Integrate new sensor modalities, such as tactile sensing and audio, into robot foundation models alongside vision and language. Design and run empirical evaluations, writing robust code for physical hardware and simulators. Contribute to publications and open-source releases.

vacancies.title: Privacy Security Engineer, Privacy & Data Protection - Applied AI
vacancies.description:
Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Privacy and Data protection expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep privacy engineering expertise to hard, real-world problems in how systems collect, use, retain, expose, and delete data. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement.
The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. Models already handle the privacy obligations that are stated as ordinary good engineering practice, so the work is the obligation they cannot derive.

This role is for privacy engineers who want to operate at the intersection of deep privacy expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to privacy work but shaping what it is capable of.

Responsibilities:
Apply deep privacy and data protection expertise to identify, scope, and solve complex problems that require multi-step reasoning, novel approaches, and expert judgment Build privacy capabilities, tools, and evaluation environments, prototyping AI-driven solutions to real-world privacy problems at Meta's scale Design and execute privacy obligation analysis, de-identification assessment, data lifecycle review, or data access reasoning augmented by AI tools and agents Identify where AI models lack privacy reasoning capability and directly contribute to improving them through expert-generated signals, evaluation, and feedback Collaborate with model researchers to translate privacy expertise into training signals, decomposing hard problems into structured challenges that teach models to reason like privacy engineers Partner with legal, policy, product, and infrastructure teams to translate obligations into engineering requirements Own complex privacy initiatives end to end, from problem definition through delivery, and contribute to technical direction within the team Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader privacy and security community

Qualifications:
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience in technical privacy, data protection, or privacy-adjacent security engineering Deep expertise in at least one privacy subdomain with demonstrated ability to advance the state of the art: purpose limitation, retention and deletion, data access control, jurisdictional obligations, de-identification, consent, or ML and model privacy Experience implementing privacy obligations in production systems, in addition to reviewing or advising on them Software engineering proficiency, including code review and maintenance, with experience coding in Python, PHP, Java, C/C++, or an equivalent language Track record of architecting privacy systems, controls or programs that operate at scale and influence how others build Demonstrated ability to define and drive complex, ambiguous problem spaces with group-level impact Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies Experience applying differential privacy, k-anonymity, or other formal implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews) Experience implementing obligations conditioned on jurisdiction, age band, or cohort: regional carve-outs, regulatory deadlines, minor and parent-initiated request handling Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red teaming, or evaluation design Background in ML and model privacy: memorization, membership inference, training-data extractability, disclosure through model outputs Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign vacancies.title: Security Engineer, Trust & Safety - Applied AI
vacancies.description:
Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Trust & Safety expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep domain expertise in online abuse and adversarial behavior, across areas such as child safety, human exploitation, fraud and scams, violent extremism, and coordinated inauthentic behavior, to advance what AI systems can do in Trust & Safety. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement.
The problems here are the ones where abuse comes from behavior, context, and scale rather than a software defect: a model that overtrusts an asserted authorization, an agent pressured into a policy exception, a campaign in which every artifact looks benign on its own. Models recognize public benchmarks far more readily than internal ones, so building evaluations that hold up is part of the engineering process.

This role is for Trust & Safety practitioners who want to operate at the intersection of deep domain expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to protect from and prevent adversarial behavior, but shaping what it is capable of.

Responsibilities:
Identify and solve ambiguous problems within a Trust & Safety domain where the solution and requirements are initially unknown, driving solutions that affect multiple teams Architect Trust & Safety capabilities and evaluation infrastructure that set the standard across teams; drive platform-level decisions for AI-driven solutions at Meta's scale Lead the strategy and methodology for the abuse problems AI cannot yet reason about: age-aware policy boundaries, adversaries who adapt to enforcement, abuse at campaign scale, and policy interpretation under pressure Shape how Trust & Safety expertise translates into AI capability: define the methodologies that make model improvement systematic and scalable Drive cross-organizational partnerships that define how Trust & Safety and AI intersect: influence technical direction beyond the immediate team Break down problems into smaller scoped workstreams, owning the most technically complex pieces while enabling others to execute against the overall solution Mentor other engineers across the organization, build community, and act as a role model for Trust & Safety engineering practices and Meta values Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader community

Qualifications:
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience. OR PhD + 2 years of hands-on engineering experience 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience in Trust & Safety, integrity, fraud and abuse, or security investigations Demonstrated depth in at least Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement.
The problems here are the ones where abuse comes from behavior, context, and scale rather than a software defect: a model that overtrusts an asserted authorization, an agent pressured into a policy exception, a campaign in which every artifact looks benign on its own. Meta is seeking a Director of Software Engineering to join our Central Integrity team which exists to keep billions of people safe on Meta's platforms. We design and deploy systems that detect and disrupt harm at an unprecedented global scale, making this one of the largest deployments of AI for positive real-world impact anywhere in the industry. Our work safeguards critical areas including child and youth safety, fraud and scams, identity and authenticity and more while actively building defenses against novel frontier threats, such as autonomous AI agents and automated risk vectors. This represents some of the most technically demanding and high-stakes engineering and product at Meta, driven by a deeply mission-focused team. You'll combine strong engineering fundamentals with cutting-edge AI to build effective, adaptable solutions that stay ahead of evolving integrity and safety risks. If you are driven by hard technical challenges and want your work to deliver immediate, real-world impact, this is the role for you.

vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern, Low-Power Scene Reconstruction for AR/VR
vacancies.description:
Future AR and VR devices occupy ever-smaller, glasses-like form factors and thus require ever-tighter power budgets. At the same time, we require higher-quality passthrough rendering and scene understanding. In particular, depth estimation, which reconstructs scene geometry in real time from sensor signals, is one of the biggest power consumers in AR and VR devices. However, most existing work targets datacenter GPUs, or at best mobile silicon with an order of magnitude more power headroom than what glasses form factors allow.

Reality Labs is Meta's innovation engine for next-generation AR/VR and wearable technology and XR Graphics is involved in building the next-generation imaging and reconstruction stack that closes this gap. We are looking for a Research Scientist Intern to work on low-power real-time reconstruction of scene geometry for AR/VR. 

Today, VR passthrough, hand interaction, and environment understanding run on separate pipelines, each tuned for different accuracy, latency and power target. We are interested in deduplicating the compute (and thus reducing power):

- What is the right depth estimation and processing strategy, from the ground up, for a glasses power budget?
- Can we train a single lightweight scene representation that can serve passthrough, hand occlusions, and background occlusions simultaneously?

These are open questions, and you would help define the approach. This is a research internship. You will own a genuinely open problem, choose the methods, build the evaluation, and present your results, with support for publication where the work warrants it.

Responsibilities:
Plan and execute research to advance the state of the art in low-power, real-time scene reconstruction for AR/VR — spanning depth estimation, occlusion, and geometric scene understanding. Explore the extent to which a shared, learned scene representation can serve multiple downstream consumers at different latency and accuracy points. Define evaluation methodology and run experiments measuring geometric accuracy, temporal stability, rendering distortion, latency, and compute and power cost on real multi-sensor device captures. Collaborate with researchers and engineers across the passthrough, scene understanding, and on-device compute teams to assess feasibility within headset and glasses power envelopes. Document and present findings, and contribute to publications and patents where the results warrant it.

Qualifications:
Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD degree in the domain of computer vision, machine learning, computer graphics, robotics, or a related technical field Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment Knowledge and hands-on experience in at least one of: depth or stereo estimation, 3D reconstruction (TSDF, implicit or neural fields, Gaussian splatting), video or instance segmentation, or neural scene representations Experience designing and running quantitative experiments, and communicating technical results Intent to return to a degree-program after the completion of the internship Proven track record of achieving significant results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, as well as first-authored publications at leading workshops or conferences such as CVPR/ECCV/ICCV, SIGGRAPH/SIGGRAPH Asia, 3DV, ICLR, NeurIPS, etc Experience with efficient or on-device inference: quantization, distillation, pruning, or deployment to mobile NPU, DSP or GPU targets Experience with multi-sensor fusion across heterogeneous sensors — RGB, IR/CV cameras, time-of-flight — including camera calibration and cross-sensor registration Experience with temporal filtering and state estimation over scene state Familiarity with AR/VR passthrough, reprojection, occlusion rendering, or SLAM and scene reconstruction Experience with C++, and with profiling or optimizing real-time computer vision or graphics pipelines Experience working in a Unix environment Experience reasoning about compute and power budgets as a first-class design constraint

vacancies.title: Program Manager, Security Risk Program

We are building a governance, risk, and compliance function to enable our company to build
products that can withstand regulatory scrutiny, and ensure Meta continues to meet global
regulatory requirements and manage risk. Meta's Risk and Compliance Program (RCP) is the central engine driving risk management and compliance at the company, supporting Meta and the family of apps. Within RCP, the Security Risk Program (SRP) is the second-line function accountable for how Meta identifies, assesses, quantifies, and reports its security risk posture — delivering global security risk assessments, Capability Maturity & Effectiveness (CME) evaluations, AI and cloud risk assessments, and board-level and regulatory reporting.

We are seeking a Security Risk Program Manager to build one of the program's highest-priority new capabilities: security risk assessment of AI product launches. Today, AI launches receive
ad-hoc coverage through security risk assessments designed for infrastructure — not for
product-launch cadence, and not for cross-domain AI risk spanning Security, Privacy, Integrity,
and Legal. You will design that capability from the ground up and scale it from roughly five
assessments per quarter today to twenty or more per quarter by H1 2027, in step with Meta's AI
product velocity.

This is a builder and an influencer role in equal measure. AI launch risk cannot be
assessed by one function acting alone — it requires Central Security, product groups, Privacy,
Integrity, and Legal moving through a shared process on a launch timeline. You will own that
operating model: translating product and engineering reality into a defensible risk position, and
translating regulatory obligation into assessment work that product teams can actually absorb
without stalling a launch. The ideal candidate is comfortable with ambiguity, effective in
high-pressure and fast-moving situations, and able to build durable relationships across a wide
range of technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Responsibilities:
Design and implement Meta's AI Launch Risk Assessment framework end to end — intake criteria, cross-domain risk taxonomy, assessment methodology, and launch-gate outputs — and scale delivery from ~5 to 20+ assessments per quarter by H1 2027. Build and partner to manage the XFN operating model that coordinates Central Security, product groups, Privacy Risk Management, Integrity Risk Management, and Legal through each assessment, with clear roles, handoffs, and decision rights on a launch timeline. Partner directly with product and engineering teams on high-priority AI launches — engaging early enough that security risk review informs design decisions rather than gating release, and giving product teams a predictable, well-documented path through second-line review. Serve as the connection point between the Security Risk Program, Central Security leadership, Legal, and first-line business teams, representing security risk positions and negotiating assessment scope, sequencing, and remediation commitments. Build and maintain a consolidated AI risk register that gives leadership a single view of. security risk across the AI product portfolio, and produce the reporting that keeps that view current for VP and executive audiences. Define tooling requirements and drive AI-enabled automation across the assessment lifecycle — identifying where automation can scale throughput without compromising assessment defensibility, and partnering with tooling and engineering owners to deliver it. Ensure assessments and supporting artifacts are produced to internal standards, are. submission-ready, and constitute defensible evidence of systematic security due diligence for regulators and auditors (including EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF expectations). Identify risks, dependencies, and blockers across the program, define mitigation plans, monitor key delivery and SLA metrics, and drive corrective action with stakeholders when performance deviates. Create and facilitate presentations that build senior leadership understanding and influence decision-making, and provide mentorship and guidance to junior team members on program design and assessment practice.

vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern, Audio, Machine Learning and Computer Vision (PhD)
vacancies.description:
The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. And just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives.

In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality, and redefining human hearing. See more about our work here: https://tech.facebook.com/reality-labs. These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart, and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments.

Meta Reality Labs Research is looking for experienced interns who are passionate about ground breaking research in audio signal processing, machine learning and audio visual learning to solve important audio-driven problems for AR/VR applications. We currently have open positions for a range of projects in multimodal representation learning, audio visual scene analysis, egocentric audio visual learning, multi-sensory speech enhancement and acoustic activity localization. 

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities:
Research, model, design, develop, and test novel audio and speech processing algorithms using machine learning, signal processing, and computer vision. Collaborate with researchers and engineers across diverse disciplines. Design and implementation of novel algorithms to solve audio research problems. Experimental design, implementation, and execution to evaluate new audio technologies. Collaboration with other researchers across audio and acoustic engineering disciplines. Communication of research agenda, progress, and results.

vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern, PhD — Meta Superintelligence Labs
vacancies.description:
Meta was built to help people connect and share, and over the last decade our tools have played a critical part in changing how people around the world communicate with one another. With over a billion people using the service and more than fifty offices around the globe, a career at Meta offers countless ways to make an impact in a fast growing organization.

Meta is seeking Research Interns to join our AI Search research team. We are committed to advancing the field of artificial intelligence by making fundamental advances in how AI agents learn from their own experience — improving their search and reasoning workflows, retaining useful knowledge, and transferring those gains to unfamiliar tasks. A central research challenge is making repeated self-improvement reliable when feedback is sparse or noisy.

The intern will work in one of three directions, scoped closer to the start date together with the intern manager:

-Learning to improve research workflows — agents learn better search, tool-use and verification strategies from prior attempts by improving their harness: the workflow, memory, tools and feedback loop around the model. Topics include meta-learning across tasks, automated agent design, and learning from natural-language feedback.

-Persistent memory and continual learning — agents retain useful lessons and update knowledge across tasks, whether in context, in compressed memory, or in weights, without forgetting what they already know. Topics include long-context modeling, context compression, continual learning, and test-time training.

-Learning from imperfect feedback — turning noisy judgments and failed attempts into useful learning signals, and improving the strategy an agent uses to learn, including how it selects and evaluates its next improvement. Topics include reward learning, credit assignment, and learning to learn.

Across all three directions, the key test is whether improvements transfer to new tasks. The goal is to develop novel methods and experiments toward a first-author submission at a leading ML/NLP venue. Recent internships on this team have produced work such as REFRAG, a new architecture for retrieval-augmented generation.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities:
Develop novel state-of-the-art methods for self-improving, agentic AI systems, leveraging a range of deep learning and reinforcement learning techniques. Design and run experiments that test whether agent improvements generalize and transfer to unseen tasks. Perform research to advance the science and technology of intelligent machines. Help analyze and improve the reliability and robustness of the resulting methods. Disseminate and publish research results, and contribute to research that can be applied to Meta product development.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. And just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives.

In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality, and redefining human hearing. See more about our work here: Inside Facebook Reality Labs Research: The future of audio and Filter Out the Noise With Conversation Focus. These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart, and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments.

Meta Reality Labs Research is looking for an intern who is passionate about speech perception and audio quality to investigate why processed speech sometimes sounds degraded or robotic. The project focuses on identifying systematic phonemic errors as causal factors in perceived quality degradation, and linking these errors to human quality and intelligibility judgments. A core method is to explore the capabilities of audio vs video LLMs. This is fundamentally a speech-perception research role; multimodal/LLM methods are a supporting tool rather than the central focus.

Relate findings to human perceptual data (quality preference and intelligibility) and translate them into actionable insights for research and engineering teams. Where appropriate, adapt multimodal models to the task in a supporting capacity.  Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and cross-functional partners to define goals, communicate findings, and drive improvements in speech quality. Develop tools and infrastructure to streamline and scale the analysis. Stay current with research in speech perception and audio quality and intelligibility assessment, and incorporate best practices into Meta's workflows. Disseminate results through internal reports and presentations, and, when appropriate, external publications.

vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern, Robotics Foundation Models Mid-Training (PhD)

Meta Reality Labs Research is a team of researchers and engineers pushing the frontier of AI and robotics. Our team is building the next generation of world action models (WAMs) and vision-language-action models (VLAs) for robotic manipulation. We are seeking a Research Scientist Intern to develop scalable methods for mid-training world action models on large-scale egocentric video and robot data.

Interns in this role will conduct fundamental and applied research to advance foundation models for robotics, with a focus on mid-training. You will collaborate with research scientists and engineers to develop new algorithms, build and evaluate model capabilities, and contribute to the next generation of embodied AI.

Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities:
Develop scalable mid-training methods for WAMs using large-scale egocentric video and heterogeneous robot data. Investigate representation and objective design for learning from human egocentric video. Address challenges in training on web-scale, weakly-labeled data, including embodiment and viewpoint gaps, data curation and filtering, and domain mixture weighting. Build efficient training and data pipelines, and study how downstream policy performance scales with dataset size, model capacity, and compute. Design experiments and benchmarks to measure what mid-training contributes, isolating its effect on downstream post-training and generalization across tasks and embodiments. Collaborate with research scientists and engineers to evaluate mid-trained models in simulation and on real robots. Communicate research findings and publish results at leading machine learning, computer vision, and robotics venues.

Qualifications:
Currently has or is in the process of obtaining a Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, or a related STEM field Research experience in training of video models or robotics foundation models Experience implementing and training deep learning models using Python and PyTorch or a comparable framework Experience designing controlled experiments, analyzing results, and debugging machine learning algorithms Interpersonal experience: cross-group and cross-culture collaboration Must obtain work authorization in country of employment at the time of hire and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment Intent to return to degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op Experience training VLAs, WAMs, or other foundation models for embodied decision-making Experience with diffusion or flow-based policies, action-sequence prediction, or action-conditioned world models Hands-on experience with distributed training across multiple GPUs or nodes, including improving training throughput, memory efficiency, and stability Experience evaluating learned policies on physical robots or robotics simulation benchmarks Proven track record of achieving significant results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, and/or accepted papers in top conferences or journals such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, ACL, etc

We are transitioning to an agentive operating model where AI handles routine work and human experts focus on the cases, decisions, and system improvements that require judgment, creativity, and domain expertise.

You will own Meta's most complex, sensitive, and time-critical escalations, where AI reaches its limits, and expert human judgment determines the outcome. Working across all Meta surfaces, products, and issue types, you'll investigate and resolve high-stakes situations spanning civic concerns, entertainment events, advertiser integrity, regulatory risk, and AI product failures.

You'll serve as a domain expert and workflow contributor by designing how humans and AI work together, critically evaluating AI outputs, encoding your expertise into systems that scale, and supporting others to do the same. You'll lead or contribute to pods that drive measurable operational improvements.

This role is for people who navigate ambiguous situations by defining structure, identifying key decisions, and driving toward resolution, prioritize effectively across competing demands, and see AI as a force multiplier for better outcomes.

**Disturbing content:** This role requires the review of content, issues, and matters that can be offensive or disturbing, including but not limited to graphic violence, self-harm, hate speech, abuse, and sexually explicit material. Meta provides resources and support for employees who work with sensitive content.

**On call:** This role will require regular scheduled weekend and holiday oncall work, and some non-scheduled crisis intervention.

**Pace:** The work is interrupt-driven. You'll balance proactive improvement work with reactive escalation response, and the escalations take priority.

**AI Forward:** This team actively uses AI tools in its daily operations. You're expected to push the boundary of what AI can handle and know where human judgment must intervene.

vacancies.title: Optical Engineering AI and Data Analytics Intern
vacancies.description:
We are the independent measurement engine for Meta's MR hardware. Every optical claim a headset makes — how sharp it looks, whether the colour is right, whether the two eyes fuse comfortably — is something our team measures and signs off on before the product ships.
That measurement happens across roughly 80 instruments and factory stations spread over contract manufacturers in Asia, display vendors, and labs in Sunnyvale and Redmond. Those stations generate about 1.3 billion rows of test data, which flow through a pipeline we own and used across the org.

The physics is interesting, but the bottleneck is not physics. It is data. Measurements that never reach the pipeline cannot be acted on, and today a large fraction of our upstream quality data never does. That is the problem this internship is pointed at.

This is a 12 week internship.

Responsibilities:
Upstream Data Ingestion: Build automated ingestion paths and pipeline schemas to integrate previously offline lab and bench measurement data. Tool Calibration AI Agent: Develop an AI agent and system of record to track instrument certification, trigger automated maintenance alerts, and coordinate service scheduling. Production Test Analytics: Implement automated analytics layers for measurement system analysis (Gauge R&R), station-to-station correlation, and drift detection across large-scale production test data.

Qualifications:
Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field Proficiency in Python or TypeScript/JavaScript, and comfort learning the other Working knowledge of SQL and experience querying a relational or columnar data store Foundation in statistics and data modeling: distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and fitting and judging a model against held-out data Experience building something other people used, such as a tool, pipeline, dashboard, model or library. Coursework counts if the artifact was real Able to explain a technical result, and how confident you are in it, to someone who does not share your background Must obtain work authorization in country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment Intent to return to full-time degree program after completion of the internship Predictive modeling and time-series analysis: forecasting, trend and change-point detection, anomaly or drift detection, and back-testing a model before trusting it Statistical process control and measurement systems analysis: Cpk, control charts, Gauge R&R, station-to-station correlation Data modeling and pipelines: designing warehouse schemas, and distributed processing (Spark, Presto, Hive or equivalent) with ETL / pipeline orchestration Full-stack web development for data products: React / Next.js with TypeScript, server-side APIs (REST or GraphQL), and scheduled jobs Building with LLMs: agents, tool use, retrieval, or evaluation Testing and validating data products: automated checks that the numbers shown match the source data, and catching silent regressions Exposure to manufacturing, test, or instrumentation data and its usual problems: inconsistent station naming, missing metadata, silent schema drift An interest in optics or imaging. Useful, but genuinely not required

As part of the Fleet Operations, Reliability and Central Engineering (FORCE) team at Meta, the Data Center Technician Intern works alongside our technicians and engineers to support the health and reliability of Meta's global server fleet. This is a hands-on role in a live data center environment where interns learn by doing real work on real hardware, under close supervision and with structured mentorship.

The internship is a 12-week program designed for students who want to apply their coursework in a production environment at scale. Meta operates one of the largest server fleets in the world, which means the problems you work on, and the volume you see, are not something a classroom or a typical IT support role can replicate. A working familiarity with Linux, a basic understanding of server hardware, and an interest in networking fundamentals are central to this role.

Interns follow the same learning path as our full-time technicians, building proficiency in data center fundamentals, procedure execution, and hardware troubleshooting, with exposure to the diagnostic and systemic process work performed by our Production Operations engineering teams. You will have the chance to connect what you are learning in the data hall to the systems concepts behind it, and to contribute to the documentation our global teams rely on. You will work in a fast-paced environment where adaptability, attention to detail, and a safety-first mindset are key to success.

Assist with projects, including new capacity and retrofits, and repairs throughout the data center. vacancies.title: Research Scientist Intern, Audio-Visual Conversation Scene Generation (PhD)
vacancies.description:
The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. 

Reality Labs Research Audio builds the audio-visual perception that future smart glasses will rely on. That includes understanding who the wearer is talking to, who is speaking, and how a conversation is organized. To train and evaluate these models at scale, we need realistic conversation data that comes with exact ground truth. This internship explores generative models that produce such data.

The project:

Generate realistic video with audio of multi-person conversations. Inputs can be text alone, text plus one image of a group, or text plus a reference image for each person. Beyond looking real, the scenes should show natural social interaction: turn-taking, gaze, head orientation, listener reactions and group formations. Each scene should also be controllable: the 3D position of each person, how people are grouped, and the position and pose of the egocentric camera. That control is what lets the output serve as accurately labelled training data for audio-visual models, e.g. predicting the glasses wearer's intent or detecting conversation groups.

Responsibilities:
Design and train video diffusion or flow-matching models for multi-person conversation scenes, generating audio and video together. Develop ways to condition generation on 3D layout, group structure and egocentric camera trajectory. Keep each person's identity consistent across frames and viewpoints, from one or several reference images. Model natural conversational behavior: speech-driven faces and gestures, gaze, turn-taking and listener reactions. Build evaluations for realism, audio-visual sync, identity consistency, and how closely the generated 3D positions and poses match the specified ones. Use the generated data to train downstream egocentric perception models, and measure how much it helps. Publish results at top venues together with Meta researchers.

vacancies.title: Старший LLM-разработчик в команду претрейна Alice AI LLM
vacancies.description:
Претрейн — первый и самый затратный этап обучения LLM. Наша команда отвечает за скорость и стабильность обучения моделей YandexGPT. Приглашаем в команду старшего LLM-разработчика, который умеет писать классный код. Откликайтесь, даже если вы пока соответствуете не всем требованиям вакансии, но очень-очень хотите научиться новому (и уже учитесь)!

Претрейн — первый и самый затратный этап обучения больших языковых моделей (LLM). Его оптимизация даже на несколько процентов может сэкономить компании десятки миллионов рублей.

Наша команда отвечает за скорость и стабильность обучения моделей Alice AI LLM. Мы разрабатываем фреймворк для распределённого обучения на сотнях GPU, ставим много экспериментов, ускоряем и улучшаем базовые модели, которые выкладываются в open source и интегрируются в ключевые сервисы. Помимо нас, нашим фреймворком для обучения пользуются почти все LLM-инженеры Яндекса, а некоторые его части есть в открытом доступе. Например, мы можем похвастаться разработкой YaFSDP, ускоряющего предобучение на 20% в сравнении с решением от Torch.

Приглашаем в команду старшего LLM-разработчика. Откликайтесь на вакансию, даже если вы знаете не всё из перечисленного ниже, но очень хотите научиться — и уже учитесь.

Обязанности:
Повышение скорости и стабильности претрейна Alice AI LLM

Мы прокачиваем все составляющие гигантских LLM-обучений: эффективно реализуем разные виды распределённого обучения, значительно ускоряем обучение на тысячи GPU за счёт использования типов пониженной точности и самописных CUDA/Triton-кернелов, экспериментируем с архитектурой, оптимизаторами и др. У вас будет возможность поработать над разными задачами по всему стеку предобучения.

Улучшение работы с длинным контекстом

В эпоху AI-агентов и мультимодальных моделей очень важно работать с контекстами в сотни тысяч токенов. Возможность эффективной работы с контекстом такой длины ещё со стадии претрейна — большой инженерный и исследовательский вызов. Будем вместе с ним справляться.

Разработка единой кодовой базы для LLM-обучений

Мы работаем над значительным улучшением и ускорением нашей инфраструктуры обучения: дизайним и пишем с нуля модули, которые будут использованы по всему стеку обучения — от претрейна до алаймента и мультимодальных обучений. Если вам всегда хотелось написать свою DL-библиотеку — это отличная возможность.

Исследования и инжиниринг в одном флаконе

Вам предстоит проводить эксперименты, изучать самые последние статьи и имплементировать даже недостающие части из них. Наша команда перенимает и улучшает наработки таких компаний, как NVIDIA и DeepSeek, и рассказывает об этом на внутренних LLM-семинарах, лекциях в ШАДе и крупных конференциях.

Больше об ML в Яндексе — в канале Yandex for ML

Требования:
* Обучали трансформерные модели на PyTorch с нуля
* Умеете писать классный код, знаете лучшие инженерные практики
* Понимаете, как устроены современные LLM

Будет плюсом:
* Имеете опыт в распределённом обучении: знаете, что такое FSDP и контекстный параллелизм
* Разрабатывали на CUDA/Triton и сможете написать backward для Flash Attention
* Классно знаете математику и можете объяснить, что такое многообразие
